questions.question: Which modern CSS property themes native checkboxes, radio buttons, and range sliders with a custom brand color?
questions.explanation: accent-color specifies the accent color for user-interface controls like checkboxes, radios, and range inputs.

questions.question: Why is the modern :user-invalid pseudo-class preferred over :invalid?
options: It only applies error styling after the user has interacted with the field, preventing red error borders on initial page load
questions.hint: Waits for user interaction before flagging errors.
questions.explanation: :user-invalid only matches when the user has attempted to interact with the control and left it in an invalid state.

questions.question: Why do form elements like <input> and <button> not inherit the body font-family by default?
options: User agent stylesheets assign specific default system fonts to form controls
HTML blocks fonts in inputs for security
questions.explanation: Browser user-agent stylesheets explicitly define native system fonts on form controls, requiring 'font-family: inherit' to override.

questions.question: Which cursor style is best practice for elements with the :disabled state?
questions.explanation: cursor: not-allowed displays a circle with a diagonal slash, signaling that the control is disabled.

questions.question: Which pseudo-class styles the label or container of an input while that input has focus?
questions.explanation: :focus-within matches an element if the element or any of its descendants currently has focus.
